mainTopic: Protecting a field from weakening, and רב יהודה's practical teachings to רבין about cress among flax, border trees, and land near a town
overview: This amud opens with the last word of an earlier discussion: in the צדקה case, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient. אביי explains that his strictness about a sharecropper changing crops is really about protecting the land, since the wrong crop order wears it out unless the field is plowed twice. On the משנה's rule that a grain field may not be planted with legumes, רב יהודה says that ruling is for ארץ ישראל, and in Babylonia it is allowed. רב יהודה then gives רבין בר רב נחמן several practical teachings. One is when picking cress from a flax field counts as גזל. Another is that fruit of a border tree goes to the side it leans toward, following רב against שמואל. The גמרא defends רב from a ברייתא that says border trees are split, explaining that it means a tree filling the whole border strip, which is divided equally. Finally רב יהודה advises against buying a field near a town, based on a teaching of רב. The גמרא challenges this from רב's own explanation of the blessings in דברים 28, which calls property near the city a blessing. רבי אבא also brings רבי יוחנן's different explanation of those blessings. The answer to the challenge comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient in the צדקה case
steps.stepSummary: The last word of the earlier argument: in the צדקה case, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: (רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) is lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes the previous discussion. In the צדקה case, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient about changing the use of the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because he is lenient there, his strict ruling about changing crops in our משנה cannot be based only on 'you changed from the agreement.' So the גמרא needs a different reason, and אביי gives one in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא who forbids the sharecropper to change crops

phrases.english: is lenient,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from before: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is lenient in the צדקה case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the comparison to the צדקה case from the previous discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's strictness about switching crops is not about simply changing from the agreement.

steps.title: אביי explains: changing crops wrongly harms the land
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reason matches the Master's farming advice: rotating crops keeps the land strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבן שמעון's reason is like the Master's. The Master said: Someone who wants his land to stay as strong as if it rested should plant wheat one year and barley the next, and one year lengthwise and the next year crosswise.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives the real reason for רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling. He bases it on a teaching of 'the Master' about how to plant without weakening the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the order of crops affects how healthy the land stays. If the sharecropper plants something other than what was agreed, he may plant out of the proper order and wear out the owner's field. So the concern is real harm to the land, not just breaking the agreement.
steps.whyThisMatters: It changes the basis of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's opinion from 'changing the deal' to 'protecting the land,' and that sets up the Babylonia and ארץ ישראל distinction later.

phrases.english: Abaye said,
Rabban Shimon's reason is like the Master's.
phrases.notes: 'The Master' here is אביי's teacher, רבה.

phrases.english: For the Master said:
One who prefers
that his land be as if lying fallow,
phrases.notes: He means he wants to use the field and still keep it as strong as if it had rested.

phrases.english: should plant it one year with wheat
and one year with barley,
one year lengthwise and one year crosswise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן כִּדְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'changing the deal' reason is ruled out, אביי gives a new reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל forbids switching crops because the wrong crop order weakens the land.

steps.title: Plowing twice removes the concern
steps.stepSummary: The rotation advice only matters if the farmer does not plow twice. If he plows twice, there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he does not plow and plow again. But if he plows and plows again, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the Master's advice. Planting out of order only hurts the land if the farmer did not plow the field twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing twice before planting keeps the soil strong, so then the crop order does not matter. This shows the whole issue is about the land's strength.

keyTerms.meaning: we have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is worried about weakening the owner's land. Plowing twice removes that worry.

phrases.english: And we only said this
where he does not plow and repeat,
but if he plows and repeats,
we have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא כָּרֵיב וְתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on the Master's farming rule from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planting out of order weakens the land only when the field was not plowed twice.

steps.title: רב יהודה teaches that grain fields may be planted with legumes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Then רב יהודה teaches רבין the opposite: a grain field may be planted with legumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: grain, he may not plant it with legumes. רב יהודה taught רבין: grain, he may plant it with legumes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It reports that רב יהודה taught רבין a ruling that seems to go against that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids a sharecropper who took a field for grain to plant legumes there. רב יהודה says it is allowed. This sets up רבין's challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: Grain, he may not plant it with legumes, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The bracketed 'etc.' just means the rest of that line continues.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda taught Ravin:
Grain, he may plant it with legumes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the explanation of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and starts on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה: a field taken to plant grain may be planted with legumes.

steps.title: רבין objects from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבין challenges רב יהודה: the משנה clearly says grain may NOT be planted with legumes.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But didn't we learn: grain, he may not plant it with legumes!
steps.whatsHappening: רבין points out that רב יהודה's ruling goes against the words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא cannot go against a משנה. So רבין is asking how רב יהודה can permit what the משנה forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: but didn't we learn (in the משנה)?

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't we learn:
phrases.notes: Here 'he' is רבין, speaking to רב יהודה.

phrases.english: Grain, he may not plant it with legumes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's ruling from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that grain fields may be planted with legumes.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says the exact opposite, word for word.

steps.title: One rule for Babylonia, one for ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that his ruling is for Babylonia, and the משנה's ruling is for ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not difficult. This is for us, and that is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה settles the contradiction by saying the two rulings apply in different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following אביי's idea that the concern is weakening the land, the answer depends on the soil. In ארץ ישראל the land is weaker, so legumes might harm it and the משנה forbids them. In Babylonia the land is strong, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: this is for us, and that is for them

steps.whatToRemember: The rule against planting legumes in a grain field depends on the land. It applies in ארץ ישראל and not in Babylonia.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Us' means the Babylonian sages and 'them' means ארץ ישראל. רב יהודה is not arguing with the משנה. He says the משנה was talking about the land there.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not difficult,
this is for us, and that is for them.
phrases.notes: 'Us' is Babylonia, where רב יהודה lives. 'Them' is ארץ ישראל, where the משנה was taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא לַן וְהָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבין's challenge from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by location: the two rulings apply in different lands.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's ruling seemed to go directly against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's ban applies to the weaker land of ארץ ישראל. רב יהודה's permission applies to the strong land of Babylonia.

steps.title: Cress growing among flax: when taking it is or is not stealing
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה teaches that cress growing in the middle of a flax field may be taken without it being גזל. But cress growing on the edges of the field is protected, and taking it is גזל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to רבין בר רב נחמן: רבין my brother, cress plants growing among the flax are not under the rule of גזל. If they are standing on the borders of the field, they are under the rule of גזל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives רבין a new practical farming rule: when it is allowed to pick plants growing in someone else's flax field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cress growing in the middle of the flax hurts the flax, so the owner is happy to have it pulled out. Taking it is like doing him a favor by weeding. Cress on the edges does not get in the flax's way, so we assume the owner wants it there, and taking it is real stealing.

keyTerms.meaning: Cress, a small plant that can grow among other crops
Borders or edges of the field

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרָבִין בַּר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to Ravin bar Rav Naḥman:
Ravin, my brother,
these cress plants growing among the flax
are not subject to the prohibition of robbery.
If they stand on the borders,
they are subject to the prohibition of robbery.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרָבִין בַּר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another practical farming teaching from רב יהודה to רבין, after the discussion of planting grain with legumes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cress among flax may be taken. Cress on the borders of the flax field may not be taken, because that is גזל.

steps.title: Once the cress is fully grown, taking it is always stealing
steps.stepSummary: If the cress has grown hard with seeds, then even cress in the middle of the flax is protected, because the damage to the flax is already done.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they have hardened into seed, even the ones among the flax are under the rule of גזל. What is the reason? Whatever damage it caused, it already caused.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה adds an exception to his rule: fully grown cress may not be taken, even from the middle of the flax.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier permission was based on helping the flax by removing the cress. Once the cress is fully grown, the flax has already been hurt, and pulling the cress now helps nothing. So the person would just be taking the owner's property, which is גזל.

keyTerms.meaning: Hardened with seed, meaning fully grown

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the cress became 'more valuable' and that is the reason. The point is that removing it no longer helps the flax, so there is no excuse for taking it.

phrases.english: And if they have hardened with seed,
then even those among the flax as well
are subject to the prohibition of robbery.
What is the reason?
Whatever damage it caused, it has already caused.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission from step 7: it applies only while the cress is still young.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fully grown cress may not be taken even from among the flax, since removing it no longer helps the flax.
steps.whatToRemember: Taking cress from among flax is allowed only while removing it still helps the flax. Once the damage is done, it is גזל.

steps.title: Fruit of border trees goes to whoever's side the tree leans toward
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה tells רבין that the trees on the border between their fields are shared by custom: each takes the fruit of the trees leaning into his own field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to רבין בר רב נחמן: רבין my brother, these of mine are yours, and yours are mine. Neighbors at a border have a custom: a tree leaning this way belongs to this side, and a tree leaning that way belongs to that side.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה tells his neighbor רבין how they will split the fruit from the trees along the border between their fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some of רב יהודה's trees lean into רבין's field, and some of רבין's trees lean into רב יהודה's field. Following the custom of neighbors, each one takes the fruit hanging over his own land, no matter whose tree it is. Neighbors are not fussy about exactly which land grew the fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Neighbors whose fields share a border

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרָבִין בַּר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to Ravin bar Rav Naḥman:
Ravin, my brother,
these that are mine are yours,
phrases.notes: He means the trees on the border between their two fields, which lean over each other's land.

phrases.english: and those that are yours are mine.
Neighbors along a border have the custom:
a tree that leans to here belongs to here,
and one that leans to there belongs to there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרָבִין בַּר רַב נַחְמָן רָבִין אַחִי הָנֵי דִּילִי דִּילָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new practical teaching from רב יהודה to רבין, this time about trees on their shared border.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit of trees near the border goes to the owner of the field the tree leans over.

steps.title: The source: רב and שמואל argue about a tree on the border
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב יהודה's rule matches רב's view in a known argument: רב says each side takes what leans toward him, while שמואל says they split the fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: about a tree standing on the border, רב said: what leans to here belongs here, and what leans to there belongs there. And שמואל said: they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב יהודה's rule: an argument between רב and שמואל about a tree standing right on the border.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says the fruit follows the direction the tree leans, which is exactly what רב יהודה told רבין. שמואל disagrees and says the two neighbors split all the fruit equally. So רב יהודה was following the view of רב.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was stated, introducing a known teaching of the אמוראים
The border strip between two fields

steps.whatToRemember: For a tree on the border: רב says each neighbor gets the side leaning toward him, and רב יהודה follows this. שמואל says they split everything.

phrases.english: As it was stated:
A tree that stands on the border,
Rav says:
what leans to here belongs to here,
and what leans to there belongs to there.
And Shmuel says: they divide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and background for רב יהודה's custom in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's rule that border-tree fruit goes to the side the tree leans toward.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רב in his argument with שמואל about a tree standing on the border.

steps.title: A ברייתא says border trees are split
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying a tree on the border is divided, which seems to refute רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: a tree standing on the border is divided. This is a refutation of רב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's view from Step 10 using a ברייתא that says border trees are simply split between the neighbors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said each neighbor takes the fruit leaning toward his own field. This ברייתא says 'they divide', which sounds like שמואל's view. So it looks like a source against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא or משנה)
The border strip between two fields

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A tree that stands on the border – they divide it.
A refutation of רב!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's side of the argument quoted in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that each neighbor takes the fruit leaning toward his own field.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a border tree is divided, matching שמואל and contradicting רב.

steps.title: שמואל explains the ברייתא to fit רב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a tree that fills the whole border strip.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל explained it according to רב: it is talking about a tree that fills the entire border.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is about a special case: a tree so wide it covers the whole border strip.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tree fills the whole border, it truly belongs to both sides, so even רב agrees it is split. רב's rule is for a normal tree that leans to one side or the other. So the ברייתא is not against רב.

phrases.english: שמואל explained it according to רב,
where it fills the entire border strip.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by narrowing the case of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be about any tree on the border, which would contradict רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a tree filling the whole border, which even רב agrees is split.

steps.title: Then why say something so obvious
steps.stepSummary: If the tree fills the whole border, of course it is split.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is it telling us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if the tree fills the whole border, splitting it is obvious, so why did the ברייתא need to teach it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree sitting fully on shared land clearly belongs to both. The גמרא assumes a ברייתא does not waste words on the obvious, so it pushes for a real new point.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (It is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 12 for making the ברייתא obvious.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tree filling the shared border is obviously split, so the ברייתא would be teaching nothing new.

steps.title: The branches lean to one side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is needed for a tree filling the border whose branches hang over one side.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where its branches hang toward one side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a tree filling the border whose branches lean more toward one field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is a real question: maybe the neighbor on the leaning side gets more. The ברייתא tells us it is still split.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where its branches hang to one side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by adding a detail that makes the ruling less obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a case detail that makes the teaching necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed obvious and pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that even when the branches lean one way, the tree is still split.

steps.title: Still, what is new
steps.stepSummary: Even with leaning branches, the ruling still seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And still, what is it telling us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again: even with the branches leaning, why would we think anything other than splitting?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tree's base is on shared land, so it seems clear it belongs to both. The גמרא wants to know exactly what mistake the ברייתא is preventing.

phrases.english: And still, what is the point of saying it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 14 as still not showing a new point.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the branches lean to one side.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tree on shared land is still obviously shared, so the ברייתא still seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Which way do we cut the tree
steps.stepSummary: One neighbor might want to split by a line that gives him more; the other can demand an equal split.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought the neighbor on the leaning side can say: divide it this way. It teaches us the other can answer: why divide it this way? Divide it that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point: the neighbor whose side the branches hang over cannot force a split that gives him most of the fruit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you split the tree along the border line, the side with the leaning branches gets more fruit. The other neighbor can say: why cut it that way? Cut it the other way, so we each get an equal half. The ברייתא's 'they divide' means a truly equal split.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why prefer that way?)

steps.whatToRemember: A tree filling the whole border is split equally, even if its branches lean to one side. This is how רב can accept the ברייתא.

phrases.english: You might have said:
that he can say to him: divide it this way,
phrases.notes: 'This way' means a split where he gets the fruit hanging over his own side, which is most of it.

phrases.english: it teaches us
that the other can say to him: what did you see
that you divide it this way?
Divide it that way!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by showing the real new point of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the mistake the teaching prevents (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The neighbor on the leaning side could insist on a split that gives him most of the fruit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The other neighbor can demand a different cut so the fruit is split equally.

steps.title: Don't buy a field near a town
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה advises רבין not to buy land near a town, based on רב's teaching about standing by a friend's ripe field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to רבין בר רב נחמן: רבין, my brother, don't buy land close to a town. For רבי אבהו said in the name of רב הונא in the name of רב: a person may not stand by his friend's field when its grain is standing ripe.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: רב יהודה gives רבין practical advice not to buy a field near a town, and supports it with a teaching of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב taught that standing and looking at someone's ripe field is forbidden; the usual explanation is that people's looking (עין הרע) can harm the crop. A field near a town is always being passed and looked at by many people, so it is at risk.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרָבִין בַּר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: רב יהודה said to רבין בר רב נחמן:
רבין, my brother,
do not buy land that is close to a town,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: for רבי אבהו said that רב הונא said that רב said:

phrases.aramaic: אָסוּר לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁיַּעֲמוֹד עַל שְׂדֵה חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: It is forbidden for a person to stand by his friend's field
at the time when it stands with its ripe grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרָבִין בַּר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another piece of advice from רב יהודה to רבין, like Step 9, on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Avoid buying land near a town, since one may not stand by another's field when its grain is ripe.

steps.title: But רב explained the city and field blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רב יהודה's advice by bringing רב's teaching on the blessings 'in the city' and 'in the field'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רבי אבא found רב's students and asked them: what did רב say about these verses, 'Blessed are you in the city and blessed are you in the field', 'Blessed are you when you come in and blessed are you when you go out'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against the advice in Step 17. It is setting up the next move: רב's explanation of these verses will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא asks 'is that so?', hinting that a teaching of רב on these blessings may not fit the advice to avoid land near a town. Here we only get the question to רב's students. The next step gives their answer, which is the actual challenge.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְתַלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: But רבי אבא found the students of רב,
he said to them:
What did רב say about these verses:
"Blessed are you in the city and blessed are you in the field,"
"Blessed are you when you come in and blessed are you when you go out"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא אַשְׁכְּחִינְהוּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְתַלְמִידֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge to רב יהודה's advice in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's advice not to buy land near a town.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the challenge will come from רב's explanation of these blessing verses, which continues in the next lines.

steps.title: רב's explanation of the four blessings
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is now quoted in full. רב explained that 'blessed in the field' means your property should be near the city, which seems to contradict רב יהודה's advice.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: This is what רב said. 'Blessed are you in the city' means your house should be close to the בית הכנסת. 'Blessed are you in the field' means your property should be close to the city. 'Blessed are you when you come in' means you will not find your wife in a doubtful state of נדה when you come home from a trip. 'Blessed are you when you go out' means your children should be like you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the teaching of רב that it brought up in the last step. This is the actual content of the challenge to רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה told רבין not to buy land near a town. But here רב himself calls 'property near the city' a blessing. So the two teachings seem to point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: Blessed are you in the city (דברים 28:3)
A doubt whether a woman has the status of נדה, which would make her forbidden to her husband

steps.whyThisMatters: Line 5 ('property near the city') is the exact line that clashes with רב יהודה's advice. The other lines are quoted because the whole teaching comes as one package.

phrases.english: And they said to him: This is what Rav said:
'Blessed are you in the city' –
that your house should be next to the synagogue.
'Blessed are you in the field' –
that your property should be close to the city.
'Blessed are you when you come in' –
that you will not find your wife in a doubtful נדה state
at the time you come home from a trip.
'Blessed are you when you go out' –
that your offspring should be like you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full wording of the רב teaching that step 18 used to challenge רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's advice not to buy land near a town
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה's advice rests on רב's teaching that one may not stand by a friend's ripe field. Yet רב himself calls property near the city a blessing. So the advice seems to clash with another teaching of the same רב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's version: a bathroom near your table, not a synagogue
steps.stepSummary: The reply is that רבי יוחנן did not explain it this way. For him, 'in the city' means a bathroom near your table, not a house near the בית הכנסת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: רבי יוחנן did not say this. Rather, 'Blessed are you in the city' means the bathroom should be near your table. But it does not mean being near the בית הכנסת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers רב's students with a different explanation of the same פסוק, in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'in the city' as a matter of everyday convenience at home, not closeness to the בית הכנסת. This shows that רב's version is not the only way to read these blessings. It does not answer the challenge to רב יהודה, because that challenge comes from רב's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: Your table, the place you eat

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לְהוּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא אָמַר הָכִי, אֶלָּא:
phrases.english: And he said to them: Rabbi Yochanan did not say this, but rather:
'Blessed are you in the city' –
that the bathroom should be near your table,
but not the synagogue.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לְהוּ: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא אָמַר הָכִי, אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the same פסוקים than רב's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, 'blessed in the city' means a bathroom near one's table, not a home near the בית הכנסת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is consistent: there is reward for steps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רבי יוחנן would not call living next to the בית הכנסת a blessing. He holds there is reward for each step you walk to a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning, since he said: There is reward for steps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי יוחנן's reading fits a rule he says elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If walking to the בית הכנסת earns reward for every step, then living right next to it means losing that reward. So for רבי יוחנן, being close to the בית הכנסת is not the blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with what he says elsewhere)
Reward for the steps taken to go to a מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the בית הכנסת is unimportant. He is saying the walk to it is valuable, so living far away gives you more reward.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning,
as he said: There is reward for steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind step 20's rejection of the בית הכנסת reading.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading of 'in the city' that leaves out the בית הכנסת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's own teaching that there is reward for steps

steps.title: רבי יוחנן on 'in the field': property split into thirds
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוחנן, 'blessed in the field' means owning three kinds of crops: grain, olives, and grapes. It does not mean having fields near the city.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Blessed are you in the field' means your property should be divided into three: one third in grain, one third in olives, and one third in grapevines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues with רבי יוחנן's explanation, now of the 'field' blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי יוחנן's 'field' blessing is about spreading one's property over three kinds of crops, not about being near the city. This is simply a different reading of the פסוק from רב's.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יוחנן's reading is a separate view. It does not answer the challenge to רב יהודה, since that challenge comes from רב's own words. The גמרא answers it on the next amud.

phrases.english: 'Blessed are you in the field' –
that your property should be divided into thirds:
one third in grain, one third in olives,
and one third in grapevines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יוחנן's explanation of the blessings after the side point in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, 'blessed in the field' means having property spread over grain, olives, and grapes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן on coming and going: leaving the world without sin
steps.stepSummary: For רבי יוחנן, 'coming in and going out' means leaving the world as free of sin as you were when you entered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Blessed are you when you come in and blessed are you when you go out' means your leaving the world should be like your coming into the world. Just as you came into the world without sin, so too you should leave the world without sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's explanation with the last pair of blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב read 'coming' and 'going' as two separate everyday blessings. רבי יוחנן reads them together as one pair: being born and dying. A person is born without sin, and the blessing is to die that way too.

keyTerms.meaning: Your leaving the world, meaning death
Your coming into the world, meaning birth

steps.whatToRemember: רב and רבי יוחנן explain the same blessings in different ways. Only רב's version says 'property near the city' is a blessing. That line clashes with the teaching of רב that רב יהודה relied on, and the גמרא answers that challenge on the next amud.

phrases.english: 'Blessed are you when you come in and blessed are you when you go out' –

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁתְּהֵא יְצִיאָתְךָ מִן הָעוֹלָם כְּבִיאָתְךָ לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: that your leaving the world should be like your coming into the world.
Just as your coming into the world was without sin,

phrases.aramaic: אַף יְצִיאָתְךָ מִן הָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא חֵטְא.
phrases.english: so too your leaving the world should be without sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה בְּבֹאֶךָ וּבָרוּךְ אַתָּה בְּצֵאתֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's explanation of the blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, 'coming in and going out' means leaving the world without sin, just as one entered it.
